answer: Sybil resistance uses stake-backed identity: each agent locks a bond listed in a public mirror, and voting power is capped per bond, so splitting one wallet into many fake agents cannot multiply influence. Each extra Sybil needs a fresh bond, and a rising penalty schedule drops them into a cost canyon where the k-th fake identity is far pricier than the first. A cedar credential earns trust only after months of honest settlement; any double-identity slashes the whole bond. Attackers pay superlinearly per new name and risk total forfeiture, making a fake crowd dearer than real cooperation.
